questions.question: Under a $(T,S)$ policy in a periodic-review inventory system, with review period $T$ and order-up-to level $S$, which description of when orders are placed and how large they are is correct?
options: Order times depend on when the position reaches a reorder level; the size is $S$ minus that level.
Order times are the multiples of $T$; the size is set by the demand since the previous review.
Order times are the multiples of $T$, and every order has the same size $S$ units.
Order times and order sizes are both fixed in advance, as in an EOQ ordering cycle.

questions.question: A $(T,S)$ policy with review period $T\ge2$, order-up-to level $S$, unlimited order size and lead time $l\ge1$ places an order at the start of review period $k$. Which equality holds right after this order, for every demand sequence?
options: $I_k=S$ for the inventory level at the start of period $k$
$Q_k=S$ for the order placed at the start of period $k$
$P_k=S$ for the inventory position at the start of period $k$
$P_k'=S$ for the inventory position at the end of period $k$

questions.question: A $(T,S)$ policy orders $Q_k=(S-P_{k-1}')\mathbf{1}\{\operatorname{mod}(k,T)=0\}$ at the start of period $k$, with $P_{k-1}'$ the end-of-period inventory position. Which policy is it when the review period is $T=1$?
options: The base-stock policy with order-up-to level $S$.
The $(Q,r)$ policy with batch size $Q=S$ and $r=0$.
An $(s,S)$ policy with reorder level $s=0$.
A policy that orders exactly $S$ units in every period.

questions.question: A $(T,S)$ policy with review period $T\ge2$ and order-up-to level $S$ reaches a review at the start of period $k$ and places the order $Q_k=S-(\cdot)$. From which quantity is the order computed?
options: The demand $D_k$ of period $k$, so that the order replaces it in advance
The position $P_{k-1}$ at the start of period $k-1$, before $D_{k-1}$
The position $P_{k-T}'$ at the end of the previous review period $k-T$
The position $P_{k-1}'$ at the end of period $k-1$, after its demand

questions.question: A shop with a high fixed cost $K$ per order compares a base-stock policy with order-up-to level $S$ against a $(T,S)$ policy with the same $S$ and review period $T=4$. Which statement about this trade-off is correct?
options: The $(T,S)$ policy orders the same total quantity, so it has the same ordering cost and the same risk of backlog.
The $(T,S)$ policy orders at most once every four periods, so it pays $K$ less often, but the position falls further before each review.
The $(T,S)$ policy places larger orders, so it can keep a lower $S$ and still have less backlog than base-stock.
The $(T,S)$ policy orders less often and, with the same $S$, also has less backlog, because its larger orders arrive together.

questions.question: A $(T,S)$ policy has review period $T=4$ and order-up-to level $S=12$. At the end of period $7$ the inventory level is $I_7'=2$ and $3$ units are on order but not yet received. How many units does the policy order at the start of period $8$?
A $(T,S)$ policy with review period $T=4$ is run over periods $k=1,2,\dots,13$, with the order rule $Q_k=(S-P_{k-1}')\mathbf{1}\{\operatorname{mod}(k,4)=0\}$. In which periods can an order be placed?
options: Periods $4$, $8$ and $12$
Periods $1$, $5$, $9$ and $13$
Periods $5$, $9$ and $13$
Periods $3$, $7$ and $11$

questions.question: A $(T,S)$ policy has review period $T=3$ and order-up-to level $S=8$. At the end of period $6$ the inventory position is $P_6'=-1$, so demand is backlogged. How many units are ordered at the start of period $7$?

A $(T,S)$ policy with review period $T=4$ and unlimited order size raises the position to $P_4=S$ at the start of period $4$. The demands are $D_4=3$, $D_5=0$, $D_6=2$, $D_7=4$ and $D_8=5$. How many units are ordered at the start of period $8$?

A $(T,S)$ policy with review period $T=3$ places an order at the start of period $6$; demand is positive in every period. Each order arrives after a lead time of $l=2$ periods, that is, an order placed at the start of period $k$ arrives at the start of period $k+l$. At the start of which period does the next order after this one arrive?

A retailer must choose between a $(T,S)$ policy (orders only in periods $T,2T,\dots$, up to $S$) and an $(s,S)$ policy (orders up to $S$ whenever the end-of-period position is at most $s$). Which situation makes the $(T,S)$ policy the natural choice?
options: The supplier can deliver in any period, and the retailer checks the inventory position at the end of every period.
Every replenishment must have the same fixed size, for example one full truckload of fuel.
Demand is very irregular, and replenishment should start in the period right after stock runs low.
Deliveries can only take place on a fixed timetable, for example a tanker that comes every three days.

questions.question: Two $(T,S)$ systems use the same review period $T$, the same lead time, unlimited order sizes and the same demands. One has level $S$ and starts with $P_1=I_1=S$, the other has level $S+c$ with $c>0$ and starts with $P_1=I_1=S+c$; nothing is on order at the start. How do their paths compare?
options: Every order is the same in both systems, and every position and level is higher by exactly $c$.
Every order is larger by $c$ in the second system, while the positions agree after the first review.
Only the first order is larger by $c$; after that the orders agree and the positions agree too.
Every order is the same, but the positions differ by $c$ only at reviews and agree between reviews.

questions.question: A $(T,S)$ policy with $T\ge2$, unlimited order size and $P_1=S$ is run on non-negative integer demands. Which statement about a positive order $Q_k>0$ and the condition that $k$ is a multiple of $T$ is correct?
options: The two are equivalent, because every review brings the position back to $S$ with a positive order.
At a multiple of $T$ the order is positive only if the inventory position has dropped to $0$ or below.
$Q_k>0$ forces $k$ to be a multiple of $T$, but a review orders nothing if no demand occurred since the previous review.
At a multiple of $T$ the order is positive exactly when the demand $D_{k-1}$ of the previous period was positive.

questions.question: A $(T,S)$ policy has review period $T=4$, order-up-to level $S=15$ and starts with $P_1=15$. The demand is $3$ units in every period. What are the orders $Q_4$ and $Q_8$ at the first two reviews?

A $(T,S)$ policy with $T=3$, unlimited order size and $P_1=S$ is run for periods $1$ to $12$; demand is positive in every period. Each order costs $K=30$. What is the average ordering cost $Kq$ per period, where $q$ is the fraction of periods $1,\dots,12$ with an order?
A $(T,S)$ policy has review period $T=2$, order-up-to level $S=7$ and starts with $P_1=7$. The demands are $D_1=1$, $D_2=2$ and $D_3=3$. How many units are ordered at the start of period $4$?

A $(T,S)$ policy has review period $T=3$ and order-up-to level $S=8$. An $(s,S)$ policy orders $S-P_{k-1}'$ at the start of period $k$ exactly when $P_{k-1}'\le s$. Can the $(3,8)$ policy be written as an $(s,8)$ policy for some reorder level $s$?
options: Yes, with $s=7$, since every order of the $(3,8)$ policy brings the position back to $S=8$.
Yes, with $s=5$, since an order follows whenever the position has dropped by $T=3$ units.
No: an $(s,8)$ policy orders the fixed batch $8-s$, whereas the orders of the $(3,8)$ policy vary with demand.
No: with $P_2'=5$ it orders in period $3$, and with $P_3'=5$ it orders nothing in period $4$.

questions.question: Two runs of a $(T,S)$ policy with $T=3$, unlimited order size and $P_1=S$ face demand sequences that agree from period $6$ on but differ in periods $1$ to $5$. Which statement about their inventory positions $P_k$ is correct for every such pair?
options: The positions differ in every period by the difference of the total demands of periods $1$ to $5$.
The positions still differ in periods $6$ to $8$ and agree only from the review in period $9$ on.
The positions agree for all $k\ge6$, because the review in period $6$ sets both to $S$.
The positions agree for all $k\ge6$ only if the total demands of periods $1$ to $5$ are equal.

questions.question: A $(T,S)$ policy with $T=2$, $S=10$ and a maximal order size of $5$ orders $\min\{5,S-P_{k-1}'\}$ at reviews. It starts with $P_1=10$; the demands are $D_1=7$, $D_2=1$ and $D_3=1$. How many units are ordered at the start of period $4$?

A $(T,S)$ policy with $T=4$ faces demand $3$ in every period and lead time $l=2$ (an order placed at the start of period $k$ arrives at the start of period $k+2$). It starts with $P_1=I_1=S$ and nothing on order. What is the smallest $S$ for which the end-of-period level $I_k'$ is never negative?
